sources.entry: granian - A Rust HTTP server for Python apps built on Hyper and Tokio, supporting WSGI/ASGI/RSGI.

summary.one_liner: Granian is a Rust-based HTTP server for Python web applications, built on Hyper and Tokio, that serves ASGI, RSGI and WSGI apps over HTTP/1 and HTTP/2.
summary.what_it_does: Granian runs Python applications behind a Rust HTTP stack (Hyper and Tokio), and is started from a CLI with an app target such as main:app and an --interface option (asgi, asginl, rsgi or wsgi). It supports HTTP/1 and HTTP/2, HTTPS and mTLS, and websockets. It can serve static files directly without calling the Python app, and provides a multi-worker process model with options for workers, blocking threads, backpressure, runtime mode and event loop choice (asyncio, rloop, uvloop, winloop). It also includes Prometheus metrics export, worker respawn on lifetime or memory limits, access logging, and proxy-header wrapper utilities for ASGI and WSGI apps. Free-threaded Python is supported experimentally, and an embeddable async server is available for use inside existing event loops.
use_cases: serve a Python ASGI or WSGI web app over HTTP/2
run a Python app with HTTPS or mTLS
serve static files alongside a Python application
expose Prometheus metrics from a Python web server
embed an async HTTP server inside an existing asyncio program
replace a Gunicorn plus uvicorn setup with a single package
notable: Single package serving ASGI, RSGI and WSGI applications
Static file serving offloaded to the server without invoking Python
Backpressure limiter at the per-worker accept loop
Worker respawn based on lifetime, max RSS, or failures, with Prometheus metrics
Embeddable async server for running inside an existing event loop
caveats: Not a pure Python solution, and the README notes it is not ideal for applications relying on trio or gevent
Free-threaded Python support is experimental and discouraged in production; the embeddable server is also experimental and limited to async protocols with a single worker
Some respawn options on Linux with multiple workers require kernel 5.14 or newer and a sysctl setting
